name: indirect object pronouns
title: Spanish Indirect Object Pronouns Practice: Me, Te, Le, Nos, Les
description: Practice Spanish indirect object pronouns: me, te, le, nos, les, where they go, le with a + person, verbs like dar and decir, and 10 sentences checked as you tap.
answer: Indirect object pronouns say to whom or for whom something happens: me, te, le, nos, les. They go before a conjugated verb (le escribo) or attached to an infinitive, a gerund or an affirmative command (quiero escribirle, dime). Spanish usually keeps le or les even when a + the person appears: le doy el libro a Marta.

rulesCaption: Indirect object pronouns and where they go

rules.example: Me compras pan. Te escribo mañana.
Le doy el regalo a mi madre.
Les digo la verdad a mis padres.

rules.use: Attached to infinitive, gerund or command
rules.example: Voy a mandarle un mensaje. Dime.

quiz.why: A mis primos is plural: les.

quiz.after: prestas tu calculadora? La mía no funciona.
quiz.why: You lend it to me: me.
To Daniel is the indirect object: le, not lo.
Attached to the infinitive and indirect: escribirle.

quiz.after: digo a ustedes que la tienda cierra a las nueve.

quiz.why: Attached to an affirmative command: dime.
Gustar-type verbs take indirect pronouns: le encantan.

mistakes: Using lo or la for the person who receives: «lo di el libro» should be «le di el libro».
Leaving out le when a + person is there: «doy el regalo a Ana» is understood, but «le doy el regalo a Ana» is the normal Spanish.
Putting the pronoun between the verbs: «voy a le escribir» should be «le voy a escribir» or «voy a escribirle».
Writing les for the thing: «les compré» means I bought (something) for them; the thing needs its own word or pronoun.
Using le for a plural person: «le digo a mis padres» is common in speech, but «les digo a mis padres» is the standard.

heritage: Many heritage speakers say «le dije a mis papás», with singular le for a plural, because it is very common in speech across Latin America. It is understood everywhere, but formal writing and exams expect les. Also check the accent when you add a pronoun to a gerund: preparándoles.
teacher: Run a quick gift exchange with paper slips: each student says ¿Qué le das a Kevin? Le doy un libro. Then report the whole group with les: Les damos regalos a todos.

faq.question: What is the difference between le and lo?
faq.answer: Le is indirect: the person who receives something (le doy el libro). Lo is direct: the thing or person that receives the action directly (lo veo, lo compro). If you can add «to» or «for» in English, it is usually le.

faq.question: Why do Spanish speakers say le and a + person together?
faq.answer: It is called pronoun doubling. With indirect objects, Spanish normally keeps the pronoun even when the person is named: le escribo a mi madre. It sounds incomplete without le.

faq.question: Where does the pronoun go with two verbs?
faq.answer: Before the conjugated verb or attached to the infinitive or gerund, never in the middle: le voy a llamar or voy a llamarle; les estoy hablando or estoy hablándoles.
